projects.name: SUB:3 Running
beats: Context
SUB:3 takes its name from the ultimate marathon milestone — breaking the three-hour barrier. A number that represents obsession, discipline, and belief in what the body can endure.
Idea

The brand was built around this fixation with time. Seconds are stretched, distorted, repeated — a visual language drawn from race clocks and digital readouts. 02:59:99 becomes an icon of possibility.
Craft

Typography bends under pressure; mantras loop across surfaces. Packaging, apparel and campaign material look more like race posters than nutrition branding — designed to live on the street, in clubs and at the track.
Position
More than fuel: a culture. A rallying point for those who run against the clock — and win.

projects.name: Dopa Donburi
projects.lede: Wake from death, return to life.
projects.cred: Illustration by Andrew Yee · Featured: It’s Nice That, The Brand Identity, Eat Drink Design Awards
beats: Context
Approached by the team behind Devon — an international café chain with a cult following — to develop an identity for a Japanese-inspired restaurant in Sydney’s newest dining district, Darling Square.
Challenge
Something fresh, unexpected and distinctly Japanese — while building a practical, recognisable identity system that could extend easily across locations.
Idea

The Japanese motif of transformation, and DOPA — a shortened form of ‘dopamine’ — as an allegory for the chemically transformative experience of eating good food. The idiom 起死回生 (kishi kaisei, ‘wake from death, return to life’) informed a distinct typographic style.
Craft

Manga-inspired illustration and patterns commissioned from Andrew Yee. Photography and menu art direction kept clean and minimal to give the brand elements space to breathe; a palette informed by the interior; a suite of striking contemporary signage.
Recognition
It’s Nice That · The Brand Identity · Eat Drink Design Awards.

projects.name: GellaFrenda
beats: Context
A modern cucina combining a refined Italian menu with Australian hospitality. Cultural harmony sits at the heart of the identity, in keeping with Matt Woods’ striking interior design.
Idea
The name ‘GellaFrenda’ originates from Italo-Australian dialect, where modern Italian words are influenced by English to create a brand new lexicon.
Craft

Typical Italian elements — terrazzo, a brick-lined archway — combined with symbols of Australiana: gum-tree textures, native flowers. A green, red and purple palette across menus, uniforms and merch, extended into graphics for GellaFrenda Nextdoor.
Type
Lineto’s Valentine — a considered reconstruction of the original Valentine typewriter — doing justice to Italy’s inherent romance and its history of design.

projects.name: Macabalm
beats: Context
Approached by Australian actress and model Pia Miller to bring to life her vision for a transparent, natural, macadamia-based skincare product.
Idea
A name and a solid identity framework championing organic ingredients, ethical sourcing and sustainability — imbued with Pia’s own personality and values.
Craft

A visual language and tone of voice expressing the brand’s core values — natural, minimal, conscious — with a simple, clean contemporary edge, delivering the message to its market at a higher-than-average price point.

projects.name: Fish Fish
projects.strap: Aussie fish & chips, with a wink
projects.lede: Sandy toes, twilight fishing and chicken-salt sprinkled chips.
beats: Context
A playful project with nostalgic appeal: a memorable identity to hook local customers and potential franchisees, whilst celebrating the shop’s 20-year heritage.
Idea
A vibrant green-gold palette emulating the energy of Australian summer — sandy toes, twilight fishing and chicken-salt sprinkled chips.
Craft

A watermark inspired by an aquatic fin — sharp, pointed, intriguing — reflecting on itself as a dinghy’s reflection bounces over water; two wave-like patterns across takeaway packaging, signage, menus and merch; a spirited fisherman in singlet, boardies, thongs and award-worthy ’stache.
Extension
After observing the cult-like status of the housemade seasoning, we conceptualised Chook Salt — destined for hot chips nationwide.

projects.name: Our Boy Roy
projects.strap: A neighbourhood deli, big on cheer
beats: Context
Never short of neighbourhood cheer: a deli and café in Adelaide serving generous sambos, batch brew and tasty small goods in the ’burbs.
Idea

A community-driven space paying homage to Aussie deli culture — the name Our Boy Roy symbolic of cheerful, dependable energy, personified by the larger-than-life character of Roy, inspired by old-school newspaper illustrations.
Craft

Roy wears many hats, honouring the deli’s diverse offering; interchangeable pants and hairstyles repeat across menus, coffee cups, sandwich wrap and salami packaging — paired with bold signage, mix-and-match textures, a bright palette and a streetside mural.

projects.name: Tsukiyo
projects.lede: The moon’s movement across the sky.
beats: Context
A modern Japanese street food concept bringing the electric atmosphere of Osaka’s Dotonbori district to Sydney — the vibrant nights, authentic flavours and scents of its bustling streets.
Challenge
Combining Japanese street culture and tradition with a modern twist, to give Tsukiyo a unique identity in Sydney’s competitive food scene.
Idea
A moon icon in the logo, with rotating typography representing the moon’s movement across the sky.
Craft
Neon signage paying tribute to the iconic streetlights of Osaka; custom takoyaki boxes with graphics and colours echoing dining under the glow of neon.

projects.name: Willing Distillery
beats: Context
The first family-owned distillery and bar in the perfect place for a G&T — Darwin. Classic copper pots, locally sourced native botanicals, a traditional one-shot distillation process.
Idea
A brand that resonates with the Territorian people: ‘Historical Evolution’, starting from a reimagining of the Willing family crest.
Craft
Or Lemmen — a modern take on early 20th-century Antiqua — paired with Quadrant Mono by Australian designer Vincent Chan: a balance of contemporary and heritage with an Australian flair.
Position
‘Made in Darwin’ shown proudly, with archival images evoking nostalgia — a brand reflecting the community’s pride in the Territory.

projects.name: Lucky Boy
beats: Context
A takeaway Chinese spot bringing a nostalgic touch to modern Sydney — reimagining the Chinese takeaway joint with mass appeal for potential franchisees and locals alike.
Idea
A playful mascot — Lucky Boy — with a noodle bowl perched on his head, reminiscent of classic Chinese food memories.
Craft

Bold English and Chinese characters paired with a vibrant palette inspired by traditional Chinese lanterns; good fortune and luck highlighted throughout, inviting customers to dine joyfully in a modern setting.

projects.name: Microsoft Technology Centre
projects.cred: With interior architects Tom Mark Henry
beats: Context

Working closely with interior architects Tom Mark Henry on a signage and wayfinding system for the newly developed Microsoft Technology Centre in Martin Place — front-of-house entry, a customer technology centre and a series of temporary touch-down spaces.
Challenge
A suite of unique signage touchpoints reflecting the use of each individual space.
Idea
Allowing unexpected experiences to reframe everyday routine and promote creative thought.
Craft
A deep respect for the material finishes and natural palette throughout the centre — each new experience still part of a cohesive whole.
